title: Revert reliance on owning window for omni chat
body:
In screencast mode the mouse indicator was offset when hovering the omni chat input (an auxiliary window), while tracking correctly in other aux windows.

## Description

The single `mouseMarker` in `ToggleScreencastModeAction` was always parented to `layoutService.activeContainer`. Mouse listeners fire for events from any window and position the marker using the event's `clientX`/`clientY`, which are relative to the originating window.

The omni chat input window deliberately keeps the **main** window active while it is shown (unless it holds focus). So hovering it left `activeContainer` pointing at the main window while the coordinates came from the omni window — placing the marker in the wrong container with mismatched coordinates. Other aux windows don't reroute the active window, so they were unaffected.

- **`src/vs/workbench/browser/actions/developerActions.ts`** — on each mouse event, re-parent the marker to the container of the window where the event originated before positioning:

```ts
const targetContainer = layoutService.getContainer(getWindow(e));
if (mouseMarker.parentElement !== targetContainer) {
    targetContainer.appendChild(mouseMarker);
}
```

This is a general correctness fix rather than an omni-specific special case.

title: Agents window: disable-model-invocation: true prevents manual slash invocation of Agent Skills
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->

<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->

<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->

<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->

<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No — reproduction requires GitHub Copilot Chat / the Agents window

* VS Code Version: 1.133.0
* OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise

## Description

In the VS Code Agents window, an Agent Skill with `disable-model-invocation: true` appears in the `/` command menu, but manually invoking the skill does not load or execute it.

The same skill can be manually invoked successfully in regular VS Code GitHub Copilot Chat.

If I remove `disable-model-invocation: true` from the skill and start a new Agents-window session, the skill becomes invokable there.

This appears inconsistent with the intended behavior of `disable-model-invocation`: the setting should prevent model-initiated invocation while still permitting explicit user invocation.

## Test skill

I reproduced this with a simple `wait-what` skill installed at:

```text
C:\Users\<user>\.agents\skills\wait-what
```

The directory is a normal directory, not a symlink or junction.

Its `SKILL.md` contains:

```yaml
---
name: wait-what
description: Stop. That last message did not land — re-pitch it.
disable-model-invocation: true
---
```

## Steps to Reproduce

### Regular GitHub Copilot Chat

1. Ensure the `wait-what` skill contains `disable-model-invocation: true`.
2. Open regular GitHub Copilot Chat in VS Code.
3. Type `/`.
4. Select or type `/wait-what`.
5. Observe that the skill is invoked successfully.

### Agents window

1. Open the VS Code Agents window.
2. Start a new Copilot session.
3. Type `/`.
4. Observe that `wait-what` appears in the command list.
5. Select or type `/wait-what`.
6. Observe that the skill is not loaded/invoked.

The skill exists on disk, but the Agents-window session does not expose it as an available skill.

### Remove `disable-model-invocation`

1. Remove this line from `SKILL.md`:

```yaml
disable-model-invocation: true
```

2. Start a new Agents-window Copilot session.
3. Invoke `/wait-what` again.
4. Observe that the skill can now be loaded/invoked.

No other change to the skill is required.

## Expected Behavior

With `disable-model-invocation: true`:

* the skill should remain visible in the `/` menu;
* the model should not invoke it automatically;
* an explicit user `/wait-what` invocation should load and execute the skill.

## Actual Behavior

In the Agents window:

* the skill appears in the `/` menu;
* automatic model invocation is disabled;
* explicit user invocation also fails to load the skill.

Removing `disable-model-invocation: true` makes the skill usable in a new Agents-window session.

This creates a mismatch between slash-command discovery and actual skill availability in the Agents window.

## Additional Information

I verified that the skill directory is not a symlink or junction:

```powershell
Get-ChildItem "$HOME\.agents\skills" -Directory |
    Where-Object Name -eq "wait-what" |
    Select-Object Name, LinkType, Target, Attributes
```

It reports a normal `Directory` with no `LinkType`.

The key comparison is:

```text
Regular Copilot Chat
+ disable-model-invocation: true
+ explicit /wait-what
= works

Agents window
+ disable-model-invocation: true
+ explicit /wait-what
= does not invoke skill

Agents window
+ disable-model-invocation removed
+ fresh session
= works
```

## Comparison with regular Chat

The important difference is that the same manual `/wait-what` invocation works in regular VS Code GitHub Copilot Chat but does not work in the Agents window.

This suggests the problem is specific to the Agents-window / Agent Host invocation path rather than the skill itself.

## Related issues

This appears related to, but distinct from:

- #315979 — skills appear in the `/` UI but `skill()` fails for **symlinked** skills. My reproduction uses a normal directory, so that root cause does not apply.
- #316285 — Agents-window slash commands can autocomplete successfully while the execution side fails to load the corresponding prompt content. This has a similar discovery-versus-execution symptom, but concerns local Agent Plugin prompt files rather than a normal Agent Skill with `disable-model-invocation`.
- #324645 — Agent Host has had separate runtime slash-command discovery behavior from the normal VS Code chat path.

I did not find an existing issue covering this exact combination of:

`Agents window + normal Agent Skill directory + disable-model-invocation: true + manual slash invocation fails + regular Copilot Chat succeeds`.

## Description

I noticed an issue with self-defined custom agents in VS Code.

After starting VS Code, all custom agents that have `user-invocable: false` in their agent metadata are still visible in the agent dropdown and can be selected/invoked by the user.

The issue resolves itself only after opening one of the agent Markdown files and clicking into the frontmatter/header section. After that, all agents with `user-invocable: false` disappear from the dropdown as expected.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create one or more custom agent files with frontmatter similar to:

   ```yaml
   ---
   name: reviewer
   description: "Read-only reviewer agent."
   user-invocable: false
   ---
   ```

2. Restart VS Code.
3. Open the agent dropdown.
4. Observe that agents with `user-invocable: false` are visible and can be selected.
5. Open one of the agent `.md` files.
6. Click into the frontmatter/header area.
7. Open the agent dropdown again.

## Actual Behavior

After VS Code startup, agents with `user-invocable: false` are visible in the dropdown and can be invoked.

After opening an agent Markdown file and clicking into the header/frontmatter, those agents disappear from the dropdown.

## Expected Behavior

Agents with `user-invocable: false` should never be shown in the user-facing agent dropdown and should not be invocable by the user, including immediately after VS Code startup.

## Additional Notes

This looks like the custom agent metadata may not be fully applied or refreshed during startup. Opening and interacting with an agent file appears to trigger a refresh/reload that then applies `user-invocable: false` correctly.

title: agentHost: retry legacy migration when a provider cannot enumerate yet
body:
Fixes #331452

## Problem

`listChatsToMigrate()` returns `undefined` to mean *"this provider cannot enumerate its catalog yet"* (e.g. its client is still starting), not *"there is nothing to migrate"*. `_migrateLegacyProviderChats` treated the two as the same and returned. `_ensureLegacyChatsMigrated` is invoked only from `registerProvider`, and nothing re-arms it, so a single early return disabled the backfill for the entire process.

Since #329633 / #330665 made the session registry the source of truth for enumeration, this backfill is what populates a newly created registry. Losing that race meant `listSessions()` published a near-empty registry as authoritative, and `BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider._refreshSessions` evicted every cached session missing from it — sessions whose data was intact on disk.

## From the reporting user's logs

```
11:06:23.145  [Copilot] Listing chats to migrate...
11:06:25.467  [Copilot] Client unavailable while listing chats to migrate:
              Copilot startup config changed while the client was starting
11:06:25.467  [Copilot] Listing chats to migrate...
11:06:26.305  [Copilot] CopilotClient started successfully
11:06:26.434  [Copilot] Found 23 legacy sessions
11:06:30.967  [Copilot] Chat discovery: ... 1 already known to Agent Host ...
```

The migration gave up at `25.467`. One second later the same call returned all 23 sessions — but that caller was the read-only fallback in `_getSessionMetadataFromCatalog`, which does `allSessions?.find(...)` and discards the rest. Hence `1 already known to Agent Host`: of 93 sessions on disk, only the restored one reached the registry.

Corroborated by the user's database, which had `sessionRegistryBackfilled:claude` and `sessionRegistryBackfilled:codex` but not `sessionRegistryBackfilled:copilotcli`.

## Changes

- `_enumerateLegacyProviderChatsWithRetry` retries with bounded backoff instead of giving up on the first "not ready".
- `_incompleteProviderCatalogs` tracks providers whose backfill has not completed a real enumeration. It is set *before* enumerating, so a throw counts too.
- `_ensureProviderCatalogsComplete` replaces the bare `_awaitInitialProviderMigration()` call in `_computeSessions`: it awaits the initial pass, re-attempts incomplete providers **in-process**, and otherwise throws. Failing is the safe signal — `_refreshSessions` already treats a rejection as transient, keeping its cache and retrying with backoff, so no protocol change is needed.
- The migration's `register` call now uses `_retryRegistryMutation`, for parity with `_registerDiscoveredChats`.
- Per-pass logging of enumerated/registered counts.

The retry is a latency optimisation; the completeness gate is the correctness fix. A timing budget alone would still lose on a slow enough machine.

## Tests

Three regression tests: deferred-then-successful enumeration, a never-ready provider failing the listing rather than publishing an empty registry, and in-process recovery without a restart. Each fails without the production change.

`a discovery signal does not bypass completed legacy migration semantics` asserted `migrationCalls: 1, registered: []` for a provider that returned `undefined`, which encoded this bug as intended behaviour. Rewritten to keep its real purpose — a *completed* migration is not re-run — while allowing an *unperformed* one to be retried.

Typecheck clean; full node unit suite passing. Note that the tests use a mock agent, so they cover the logic rather than real provider-client startup timing.

## Notes

Affected users self-heal: the failed run never wrote `sessionRegistryBackfilled:<provider>`, so the corrected migration re-runs. This can also surface older on-disk sessions that were never registered — correct migration behaviour, but it may look like sessions appearing from nowhere.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Per-provider completeness + a catalog generation in the protocol, so clients can evict precisely instead of relying on all-or-nothing failure.
- `_computeSessions` drops registry rows when `getChatMetadata` fails or returns `undefined` — a separate pre-existing eviction vector.
- A stale in-flight list response can still race late registrations; `_registryEpoch` invalidates memoization but is not re-checked before returning.

title: Dark 2026: ordinary variables are visually indistinguishable from plain text - looks like syntax highlighting is not applied
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (the rendered colors match the built-in `theme-defaults/themes/2026-dark.json` definitions exactly, see analysis below, so extensions are not involved)

- VS Code Version: 1.133.0 (a5b5009)
- OS Version: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200

## Summary

In the Dark 2026 theme, ordinary (mutable) variables are rendered in `#C9D1D9` while the editor foreground (operators, punctuation, plain text) is `#BBBEBF`. On a dark background these two are visually indistinguishable — both read as "white". As a result, large parts of a TypeScript/JavaScript file appear to have **no syntax highlighting at all**, and my first reaction was that highlighting was broken, not that this was a design choice.

## Analysis

Measured from an actual editor screenshot (pixel-sampled) and confirmed against `2026-dark.json`:

| Token | Color | Source rule |
|---|---|---|
| ordinary variable (`process`, reassignable locals) | `#C9D1D9` | `variable.other` → `#c9d1d9` |
| editor foreground (`=`, `;`, punctuation) | `#BBBEBF` | `editor.foreground` |
| `const`-declared / readonly variable | `#79C0FF` | `constant` / readonly mapping |

The luminance difference between `#C9D1D9` and `#BBBEBF` is roughly 5% — imperceptible in practice. Notably, the theme *does* define `variable` → `#ffa657`, but the more specific `variable.other` → `#c9d1d9` rule overrides it for ordinary variables, so the orange never appears in typical JS/TS code.

This near-unstyled treatment of variables comes from GitHub Primer, where it works acceptably for snippets and diffs on github.com. In a full editor, however, variables are one of the most frequent token classes, so the effect dominates the whole file. The inconsistency with `const` variables (which do get a distinct blue) makes plain variables look even more like a rendering bug.

## Expected

Mutable variables should have a hue that is distinguishable from plain text — e.g. the `#ffa657` the theme already defines for `variable`, or something like Dark Modern's `#9CDCFE`.

## Related

- #326875 (Dark 2026 palette feels "same color in every element")
- #322000 / #320953 / #322108 (variable color change and its revert — the variable color question seems unresolved)
- Tracking: #295783

title: Reconcile external sessions in a single catalog pass
body:
## Problem

Changing `chat.agentSessions.showExternal` took **30-50 seconds** to take effect on a profile with ~600 sessions.

`_reconcileExternalSessions` walked the whole session catalog **once per mode** on a mode change, and each walk opens every registered session's database (`Limiter(4)`). The session list kept showing the old setting for that entire window.

From a real log:

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 13:49:01 | `showExternalSessions: last7Days` mirrored to the host |
| 13:49:35 | catalog pass #1 finishes (`hid 288 of 599 … 'none'`) |
| 13:49:51 | catalog pass #2 finishes → sessions finally appear (**~50s**) |
| 13:50:53 | `showExternalSessions: none` mirrored to the host |
| 13:51:30 | user opens an unrelated session |
| 13:51:32 | reconciliation finishes → **all external sessions disappear (~39s late)** |

The delayed retraction landing two seconds after an unrelated click made it look like opening a session had destroyed the list.

## Change

Derive both the outgoing and incoming visible sets from a **single** `listSessions(All)` pass. `All` is a superset of every mode and `_shouldIncludeSession` is a pure predicate over the rows, so this is equivalent. Non-mode-change reconciliations keep the plain current-mode path so they still share the in-flight list cache.

## Logging

None of the above was diagnosable from logs — nothing recorded why the mode changed, which window changed it, or how long reconciliation took. Added:

- **`RemoteAgentHostProtocolClient`** — each window logs what it mirrors into the shared host root config and from which configuration target. These keys are host-level and last-writer-wins across windows, so this identifies which window wrote a value.
- **`AgentService`** — external-sessions mode transitions (`'last7Days' -> 'none'`).
- **`AgentService`** — reconciliation duration plus published/retracted/visible counts.
- **`AgentService`** — catalog pass timing, promoted to `info` above 1s.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- A single pass over hundreds of session databases is still seconds; caching per-session metadata would remove the disk work from a mode change entirely.
- In `Recent` mode every external session `modifiedAt` change queues a full catalog pass.
- One "open session" fires three parallel `subscribe` calls that each independently attempt worktree recreation, logging the same failure 3-4 times per click.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` clean against latest `main`.
- Node unit suite: 14713 passing, 7 failing — all 7 pre-existing in `sessionPermissions.test.js` (shell-redirect path resolution), identical to the baseline run before these changes.
- Existing `AgentService` external-sessions mode-transition tests cover this path and pass.

## Summary
Keeps the dropdown half of a split action in sync with its primary action's enabled state, so a disabled split button can no longer be opened via its dropdown.

Previously, when the agent feedback editor input was empty, the primary "Add" action was disabled but the attached dropdown arrow stayed active and still opened its menu.

## Changes
- Sync the internally created dropdown action's `enabled` state with the primary action in `ActionWithDropdownActionViewItem`.
- Guard `BaseDropdown`/`DropdownMenu` against opening while disabled, covering mouse, keyboard (Enter/Space), and programmatic `show()` paths.
- Reflect the disabled state to assistive technology via `aria-disabled` on the dropdown label.
- Extend the `FeedbackInputWidget` test to assert the dropdown is inert while the input is empty and works once text is entered.

## Notes for reviewers
The behavior change lives in the shared `vs/base` dropdown primitives, so it applies to every `ActionWithDropdownActionViewItem` consumer. The new gating is opt-in via the optional `isEnabled` option and defaults to previous behavior when unset.

Same fix as #331356, targeting `main`.

## Description

After updating VS Code Insiders, I lost access to previously existing local Agent Host sessions in the Agents Window.

I will refer to the missing sessions as **Session A** and **Session B**.

Before the update, both sessions appeared in the Sessions list and could be reopened normally. On the first launch after updating VS Code Insiders, neither session appeared under Recent, Older, Archived, or in search.

The underlying conversation data for both sessions still exists on disk. Therefore, this does not appear to be conversation-data deletion. The sessions became inaccessible because they were no longer present in the Agent Host session registry used to populate the Sessions list.

## Steps to Reproduce

I do not yet have a deterministic clean-profile reproduction, but this is the sequence that produced the issue:

1. Create and use multiple local Copilot Agent Host sessions.
2. Confirm that Session A and Session B appear in the Agents Window and can be reopened.
3. Update VS Code Insiders.
4. Launch the updated version and open the Agents Window.
5. Observe that Session A and Session B are missing from Recent, Older, Archived, and search.
6. Verify that their persisted session-state folders and event histories still exist on disk.

## Expected Behavior

Updating VS Code Insiders should preserve all previously registered Agent Host sessions.

If the Agent Host registry format changes or the registry must be recreated during an update, existing sessions should be migrated or recovered from their persisted session metadata. An incomplete newly created registry should not cause existing sessions to disappear from the UI.

## Actual Behavior

After the update, previously visible sessions disappeared from the Agents Window even though their conversation data remained on disk.

There was no warning, migration error, or recovery option.

## Why This Appears to Have Happened

The diagnostics suggest the following sequence:

1. Before the update, VS Code's backed-up session index still contained Session A and Session B.
2. During the first startup after the update, a new Agent Host session registry database was created.
3. The new registry did not include Session A or Session B.
4. Startup enumerated the existing Copilot SDK sessions, but the missing sessions were not imported into the new registry.
5. The Agent Host then returned the sessions from this incomplete registry through `listSessions()`.
6. The Sessions provider treated that successful response as authoritative and removed cached sessions that were absent from it.
7. As a result, Session A and Session B disappeared from the Sessions list even though their persisted event histories were still present.

This suggests a session-registry migration or initialization regression during the VS Code Insiders update. The persisted conversation data survived, but the association needed to discover and display those sessions was lost.

## Additional Information

This may be related to #328736, but this case is different:

- It occurred locally rather than over Remote-SSH.
- The sessions were visible and usable before updating VS Code Insiders.
- The disappearance happened on the first startup after the update.
- The persisted conversation data still exists.
- The sessions appear to be missing specifically because the newly created Agent Host registry did not recover them.

title: markdown: fix: open absolute file links in Markdown editor
body:
## Summary

Fix absolute filesystem links in the experimental Markdown editor without changing standard Markdown link semantics.

- Preserve the Markdown language service's normal resolution whenever its target exists or cannot be inspected reliably.
- Fall back to an authored absolute path only when the normal target is definitely missing and the absolute candidate is definitely an existing file.
- Enable the fallback only from the experimental Markdown custom editor's user-click path; standard preview and passive rich-link resolution remain unchanged.
- Model JSON-RPC's `null` no-result response and normalize it to `undefined` at the client boundary.

## Problem

Markdown links are URI references, so a slash-prefixed link such as `/tmp/example.md` is normally interpreted as root-relative to the workspace. The Markdown language service may return that workspace-relative target even when it does not exist in order to support create-file workflows.

In the experimental Markdown editor, this means clicking a link to an existing absolute filesystem file can instead open a nonexistent workspace-relative file and show the create-file flow.

Globally redefining slash-prefixed Markdown links as filesystem paths would break portable repository links such as `/docs/setup.md`, so this change keeps normal Markdown resolution authoritative and adds a conservative fallback.

## Resolution behavior

For the explicitly fallback-enabled open call:

1. Resolve the link normally through the Markdown language service.
2. Return immediately if there is no concrete normal target, for external links, or for links that cannot safely identify an absolute filesystem path.
3. Preserve an existing normal target.
4. Preserve the normal result if its filesystem provider is unavailable or stat returns an indeterminate error.
5. Only when the normal target is definitely missing, stat the absolute candidate.
6. Use the candidate only when it definitely exists and is not a directory.

Filesystem probes distinguish `found`, `notFound`, and `unavailable`. Since this is speculative behavior, permissions failures and missing providers preserve the established result instead of breaking the click.

## Scope and safety

- A single `MdLinkOpener` is shared, but only the Markdown editor's `openLink` message handler explicitly enables the fallback.
- Passive rich-link presentation resolution never enables the fallback and performs no additional filesystem probes.
- Absolute paths are considered only for `file` and `vscode-remote` source documents.
- Remote paths retain the source scheme and authority, so they resolve on the remote filesystem.
- Untitled and virtual-workspace documents do not target the local machine.
- Explicit URI schemes—including all `file:` URIs—remain outside this fallback.
- Protocol-relative, UNC, authority-bearing, mixed-separator, and percent-encoded UNC variants are rejected before filesystem access. A post-`Uri.file()` authority check provides defense in depth.
- Drive-letter paths are considered only on Windows extension hosts, preventing relative probes on macOS, Linux, and web.
- Directories are not reinterpreted through the file-opening fallback.
- Numeric line-fragment handling remains authoritative.

The fallback checks the exact authored path. It does not infer a `.md` extension or recompute heading-name anchors. It also requires the language service to provide a normal target, so a standalone document without workspace-resolution context may remain unchanged when the language service returns no target.

## Validation

- Markdown extension TypeScript compilation: passed with 0 errors.
- Targeted ESLint across all eight modified files: passed.
- Focused desktop extension-host suite: 14 passing.
- Focused browser extension-host suite: 14 passing.
- Repository hygiene pre-commit hook: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Related discussion

Related to #307837, which discussed a similar fallback for the built-in Markdown flow. This change intentionally has a narrower scope: only the experimental Markdown custom editor opts in, while standard preview behavior remains unchanged.

Enabling external sessions can emit thousands of individual Agent Host session notifications, causing progressive UI churn. This batches renderer-facing catalog updates while keeping the session cache current.

- **Batching**
  - Debounce added, removed, and changed notifications for 50 ms.
  - Coalesce updates by session while preserving replacement semantics.

- **Ordering**
  - Flush pending notification batches before immediate catalog changes.
  - Keep internal cache mutations and listeners synchronous.

- **Lifecycle**
  - Queue batches only while public consumers are subscribed.
  - Cancel pending work when the final consumer unsubscribes.

title: agentHost: Exclude subagent chats from billed credit telemetry
body:
Addresses the review comment on #330931.

## Problem
`CopilotAgentSession` folds each subagent charge into the parent turn's `totalNanoAiu` and *also* emits the same cumulative component on the child chat. Because `agentHost.turnCompleted` recorded both channels, summing `billedNanoAiu` across events double-counted nested usage.

## Fix
Skip subagent chat channels when recording billed credits, mirroring the guard `_trackTurnUsage` already applies for the same reason. Credits stay attributed to the parent turn, which already includes the subagent cost, so the measurement remains additive.

## Validation
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostTurnTelemetry.test.ts` (25 passing)
- Confirmed the new parent-plus-subagent test fails without the guard: the subagent turn reported 1e9 that the parent's 3e9 already contained, so the sum was 4e9 instead of 3e9.

Note: this same fix ships together with the feature in the `release/1.134` backport (#331436).

title: Fix Agent Merge stalling on indeterminate pull request state
body:
## Problem

Agent Merge silently stalled: it bound to the pull request, then reported `Gate is indeterminate` roughly 40 times over 32 minutes and never looked at the CI failures or PR comments it was configured to handle.

```
23:13:11 Started session runtime: overrides=addressReviews,fixCI,mergePullRequest,resolveConflicts
23:13:20 Bound session to its pull request
23:13:35 Pull request state ready
23:13:35 Gate is indeterminate: reason=Pull request state is incomplete or stale   <- x40
23:45:07 Disabling Agent Merge: the checked-out branch changed while PR state was refreshing
```

Two independent bugs in the GitHub platform layer, both reproduced against `api.github.com`.

## Bug 1: the capability probe exceeded GitHub's introspection limit

`capabilitiesQuery` selected `__Type.fields` three times; GitHub allows two. The live response:

```
HTTP/2.0 200 OK
{"errors":[{"type":"INTROSPECTION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
  "message":"Introspection fields may only be used 2 times, but some fields were used more than that: __Type.fields (3)"}]}
```

HTTP 200 with errors means `_probe` returned `unavailableCapabilities`, which is why every log line reported `graphql=false` for **api.github.com**. Since `INTROSPECTION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` is not a schema-validation error the result was never cached, so the probe repeated forever.

That cascades through `plan()`: `reviewThreads` -> `unavailable`, `checks` -> `restChecksFallback`, `mergeability` -> `restMergeabilityFallback`, all hardcoded `complete: false`. `evaluateAgentMerge` requires all three complete, so the gate could only ever return `'Pull request state is incomplete or stale'`.

`RequirableByPullRequest` now gets an existence check rather than a field enumeration. This is exact, not a heuristic: `isRequired` is that interface's only field, confirmed against the live schema.

## Bug 2: every conditional REST GET threw on 304

```
REST GET api.github.com/repos/microsoft/vscode/pulls/331332/reviews failed (malformedResponse:304)
REST GET .../commits/d2c2865.../status failed (malformedResponse:304)
REST GET .../commits/d2c2865.../check-runs failed (malformedResponse:304)
```

GitHub may answer a conditional request with a reissued validator. Verified live:

```
200-path etag=[W/"4ee1eec6a2ddc9...2694"]
304-path etag=[  "4ee1eec6a2ddc9...2694"]
```

The literal comparison treated this as a protocol violation. It was also self-perpetuating: the stored validator was never updated, so each later revalidation resent the stale `If-None-Match` and failed identically until the cache was evicted, which stopped `checks` and `submittedReviews` from refreshing at all.

A 304 backed by a cached entry is now accepted, and the reissued ETag and Link are adopted so the next revalidation sends the validator GitHub last handed out.

## Logging

`graphql=false` is indistinguishable from a legitimately old GitHub Enterprise host, which is what hid this for so long. Probe errors that disable GraphQL are now logged (`warn` for unexpected errors, `debug` for genuine schema mismatches) with the GraphQL error type included, so `INTROSPECTION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` would point straight at the cause.

## Testing

- `stays within the GitHub introspection budget` - asserts the query never regresses past two `fields` selections
- `warns when an unexpected probe error disables GraphQL capabilities`
- `adopts a reissued validator when revalidating with a 304` - seeds `"old"`, returns a 304 carrying `W/"new"`, and asserts the *next* revalidation sends `If-None-Match: W/"new"`, proving the stored validator was refreshed rather than left stale
- `rejects a 304 that answers no cached representation` - keeps the genuine protocol violation covered

90 tests pass in `vs/platform/github/test/node`, 15 in the agent merge suites, and `typecheck-client` is clean.

title: Recover chats with inaccessible vision history
body:
Fixes #331428

Restored chats can replay an uploaded historical image after its attachment URL
is no longer accessible. CAPI returns `vision_attachment_not_accessible`, but
Agent mode currently retries the unchanged request and later turns replay the
same stale image.

This change:

- Classifies `vision_attachment_not_accessible` consistently for HTTP and
  WebSocket responses.
- Prevents generic Agent mode retries for only this error code.
- Retries once without the historical image set implicated by the failed
  request.
- Closes stale WebSocket state and resubmits the complete cleaned request.
- Persists SHA-256 hashes of unavailable image sources in existing turn
  metadata, never raw URLs or image bytes.
- Omits only matching historical sources after restoration.
- Preserves images attached after recovery.
- Preserves existing behavior for unrelated bad requests, server failures,
  and network failures.

The backend error does not identify which image failed. When several historical
images were present in the failed request, the recovery conservatively
quarantines that historical image set.

This PR does not make uploaded attachment URLs durable. A complete storage fix
would retain durable attachment identity or image bytes and regenerate URLs
when restoring history. That requires separate decisions about retention,
privacy, session size, migration, and VS Code/Copilot ownership.

Validation:

- Reproduces a restored-history request containing an inaccessible image.
- Proves the clean retry succeeds without replaying that image.
- Proves a later turn remains usable.
- Proves recovery metadata survives conversation restoration.
- Proves images added after recovery remain available.
- Covers HTTP and WebSocket recovery.
- Confirms unrelated `BadRequest` retry behavior remains unchanged.
- Confirms server and network retries remain unchanged.
- 119 focused tests pass.
- Extension TypeScript check passes.
- Scoped ESLint passes.
- `git diff --check` passes.

Type: Bug

## Summary

Copilot Chat rendered internal edit/file URI markers directly in the Chat view instead of converting them into the expected file/edit UI blocks.

The visible output contained raw tags like:

```html
<vscode_codeblock_uri isEdit subAgentInvocationId="call_hOXkInry8cfbhIn0VAQOyQXS">file:///c%3A/Users/fenzho/code/github/java-migration-copilot-samples/asset-manager/README.md</vscode_codeblock_uri>
```

This appeared alongside several empty gray placeholder blocks in the Chat response.

## What I Saw

During a Copilot Chat agent workflow using subagents, the Chat UI displayed raw internal tags for files that had been read or edited by a subagent:

```html
<vscode_codeblock_uri isEdit subAgentInvocationId="call_hOXkInry8cfbhIn0VAQOyQXS">file:///c%3A/Users/fenzho/code/github/java-migration-copilot-samples/asset-manager/README.md</vscode_codeblock_uri>

<vscode_codeblock_uri isEdit subAgentInvocationId="call_hOXkInry8cfbhIn0VAQOyQXS">file:///c%3A/Users/fenzho/code/github/java-migration-copilot-samples/asset-manager/web/src/main/java/com/microsoft/migration/assets/config/RabbitConfig.java</vscode_codeblock_uri>

<vscode_codeblock_uri isEdit subAgentInvocationId="call_hOXkInry8cfbhIn0VAQOyQXS">file:///c%3A/Users/fenzho/code/github/java-migration-copilot-samples/asset-manager/worker/src/main/java/com/microsoft/migration/assets/worker/config/RabbitConfig.java</vscode_codeblock_uri>
```

Screenshot is available if needed.

## Expected Behavior

The Chat view should render these as normal file/edit UI elements, file pills, or clickable file references.

The internal `<vscode_codeblock_uri ...>` wrapper should not be visible to the user.

## Actual Behavior

The raw internal tags were shown directly in the Chat response, mixed with empty gray placeholder blocks.

This made the Chat output look malformed and hard to read.

## Relevant Details

- The issue occurred during a multi-agent Copilot Chat workflow.
- The visible `subAgentInvocationId` was `call_hOXkInry8cfbhIn0VAQOyQXS`.
- The files shown in the raw tags were files that the subagent read or edited during the workflow.
- The subagent's final returned text was normal Markdown and did not contain the raw `<vscode_codeblock_uri>` tags.
- The raw tags appear to come from Chat UI rendering of subagent edit/file blocks, not from the model's final response text.

## Debug Evidence

The session logs show:

1. The parent coordinator invoked a subagent with id `call_hOXkInry8cfbhIn0VAQOyQXS`.
2. The subagent performed file operations involving `README.md`, `web/src/main/java/com/microsoft/migration/assets/config/RabbitConfig.java`, and `worker/src/main/java/com/microsoft/migration/assets/worker/config/RabbitConfig.java`.
3. The subagent's final result returned to the parent was normal Markdown summary text.
4. Before investigating this issue, the transcript did not contain `vscode_codeblock_uri` as ordinary assistant text. This suggests the raw tags were exposed by the Chat rendering layer rather than generated by the agent as user-facing text.
5. There was also a later parent execution-coordinator cancellation (`Agent error: Canceled`), but the raw tag display appears tied to rendering of subagent edit/file UI blocks rather than the final subagent response.

## Environment

- OS: Windows x64
- VS Code: 1.133.0 (`a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960`)
- VS Code Chat session id: `ab17eca0-d8a9-432a-ad83-9fb63d53d9c5`
- Workflow involved Copilot Chat subagents and file edit/read tool calls.

I can provide the relevant Copilot Chat debug logs if needed.

title: Copilot retries deterministic inaccessible-image HTTP 400 four times
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.61.0
- VS Code Version: 1.133.0
- OS: Windows 11
- Feature: Agent mode with auto-approve
- Error: `400 vision_attachment_not_accessible`

## Summary

When a restored chat contains a stale or expired image reference, the backend returns `vision_attachment_not_accessible`. Agent mode classifies the response as retryable and resends the unchanged request three additional times. The same restored session repeats the four-attempt failure on later clean turns.

This report is specifically about retry classification and recovery UX. Existing issues already cover image expiration and durable attachment persistence: #313973, #295731, and #314556.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Resume an older image-bearing chat whose image asset is no longer accessible.
2. Send a new text-only turn with no explicit attachment.
3. Observe HTTP 400 `vision_attachment_not_accessible`.
4. Agent mode logs automatic retries 1/3, 2/3, and 3/3, producing four failed requests total.

## Expected

`vision_attachment_not_accessible` is deterministic for an unchanged request and should not trigger connectivity probing or automatic resend. The client should preserve the error and offer recovery such as removing the unavailable image or asking the user to reattach it.

## Actual

One text-only turn produces four failed requests: the initial request followed by three automatic retries of the unchanged request. No response succeeds, and the inaccessible historical image remains eligible for replay on the next turn.

## Likely code paths

- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompt/node/chatMLFetcher.ts`
  - Generic HTTP 400 currently falls through to `ChatFailKind.Unknown`.
  - Unknown WebSocket CAPI codes, including `vision_attachment_not_accessible`, become `ChatFailKind.ServerError`.
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/intents/node/toolCallingLoop.ts`
  - `shouldAutoRetry()` retries nearly every non-success response in auto-approve/autopilot, including `BadRequest`.

## Related issues

- #313973: image asset expiration / inaccessible attachments
- #325232: restored chat repeatedly fails and retries; closed as duplicate
- #295731: screenshots are not durably restored
- #314556: session-scoped local binary resource persistence

This report is narrower: deterministic attachment bad requests should not be automatically retried unchanged.

title: [BUG] Custom Endpoint context window size is bloated by +16K in UI & context manager, causing potential backend context overflow
body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.41 (2026-03-25) GitHub Copilot updates for [VS Code 1.113](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_113):
- VS Code Version: 1.133.0
- OS Version: Windows 11 25H2
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): agent
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Custom Endpoint
- Logs: 

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Configure a local custom endpoint (e.g., `llama-server`) with a fixed context window limit (e.g., `-c 212000` or via extension settings).
2. Observe the reported model context limit in the UI and the Session Info panel.

---

### Description / Expected vs Actual Behavior

**Issue Summary:**
When using Custom Endpoint configurations, there is a consistent discrepancy where the total context window size shown in the UI (and used by the context manager) is larger than the user-configured or server-reported value by exactly **16,384 tokens (~16K)**.

**Examples:**

* Configured: `128000` $\rightarrow$ UI Displays & Manages: `144K` ($128000 + 16384 = 144384$)
* Configured: `212000` $\rightarrow$ UI Displays & Manages: `228K` ($212000 + 16384 = 228384$)

**Core Concern & Risk:**
It is unclear whether VS Code's context manager intends to **keep display logic unified while separating input/output tokens in management**, or if **both display and management are merged together**.

* **If Input and Output limits are merged into a single hard cap:** The context manager may allow the input prompt to grow up to the full `228K` limit. When the server processes this request, the total prompt + max output generation will exceed the server's actual limit (`212000`), leading to `Context Overflow` or `400 Bad Request` errors on local inference servers (like `llama-server` / `vLLM`).
* **If they are managed separately:** The UI calculation should be clarified or aligned with the endpoint's strict maximum input capacity to avoid user confusion.

**Request:**
Please investigate how `maxInputTokens` and `maxOutputTokens` are handled for Custom Endpoints, and ensure the context manager does not allow total context length (Prompt + Response) to exceed the server-reported limit.

title: Preserve session type when splitting a Chat Editor
body:
Fixes #331422

### Problem

Splitting a Chat Editor (`View: Split Editor`) that hosts a running agent-host session produced a new pane with an **invalid chat input state** — the Agent Mode (`Interactive`/`Plan`) picker was missing and permission controls were wrong.

### Root cause

`View: Split Editor` duplicates the editor via `ChatEditorInput.copy()`, which returned a **generic `vscode-chat-editor:` placeholder** with no session type. `ChatEditor.setInput()` reads the session type **before** resolving the input; the placeholder classifies as `local`, so the widget is `unlockFromCodingAgent()`ed. The input then resolves into a **new agent-host session**, but the lock decision is never revisited, so the `chatIsAgentHostSession` context key stays `false` and the Agent Mode picker (gated on it) is filtered out.

The working `Ctrl+N` / New Chat path (`clearChatEditor`) avoids this by replacing the editor with a **typed** URI up front, so `setInput()` sees the real type before resolving.

### Fix

Make `ChatEditorInput.copy()` mint a new **untitled URI of the source pane's own session type** (local or agent-host), so a split reproduces the source harness (Claude → Claude, Copilot → Copilot, Codex → Codex) and `setInput()` locks the widget correctly before rendering. When the source type is unknown or cannot start a new session, it falls back to the previous generic URI.

Also extracts a shared `getNewChatSessionResource(sessionType)` helper into `chatUri.ts` and reuses it from `clearChatEditor` and the default session-resource helpers in `constants.ts`, removing three copies of the same URI-construction logic.

### Scope

- New split panes start an **empty** chat of the same type (they do not fork the source conversation's live model/mode/permission overrides).
- This does not change the pre-resolve behavior of `ChatEditor.setInput()` for other entry points (Move Chat to window, Import); those remain as-is.

### Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passes.
- Unit tests: `ChatEditorInput` suite — 7 passing, including 3 new regression tests (agent-host source → distinct same-type untitled URI; local source → new local session; guard-false → generic fallback).
- Manual: split Copilot / Claude / Codex editors → same type + Agent Mode picker + correct permissions; split a local chat → stays local.

## Feature request

Please expose the existing **Editing / Locked** mode toggle in the Markdown Editor (`vscode.markdown.editor`) as a VS Code command that can be assigned in Keyboard Shortcuts / `keybindings.json`.

A default keybinding is not required. A command for toggling the mode of the active Markdown Editor would be enough.

## Motivation

I frequently switch between reading and editing rendered Markdown.

In **Editing** mode, clicking a rendered block reveals its Markdown syntax and can change the document layout. When I am mainly reading or reviewing a document, I prefer **Locked** mode because the rendered view stays stable.

However, switching between Editing and Locked currently requires using the mode toggle in the UI.

The toggle itself can be reached through keyboard focus navigation, but there is no dedicated VS Code command that I can bind directly to a shortcut.

This is also useful in the Agents window, where range-based Agent Feedback is available in Locked mode, so my workflow often becomes:

```text
Editing
  ↓
Locked
  ↓
Editing
```

Being able to switch directly from the keyboard would make this workflow much smoother.

## Current behavior

- The Markdown Editor has a UI toggle for Editing / Locked.
- I could not find a dedicated VS Code command for this mode toggle.
- `markdown.preview.toggleLock` controls the existing Markdown Preview and does not toggle the Markdown Editor's Editing / Locked mode.
- `workbench.action.files.toggleActiveEditorReadonlyInSession` controls the file-level read-only state and is separate from the Markdown Editor's Editing / Locked mode.
- #329414 registers Markdown Editor commands as VS Code commands so that their shortcuts can be customized, but the Editing / Locked toggle is not currently exposed as one of these commands.

## Expected behavior

Expose a command that toggles the active Markdown Editor between Editing and Locked mode.

For example (command name only illustrative):

```text
markdown.editor.toggleLocked
```

Users could then assign any keybinding they prefer.

## Related

- #326250 — Markdown Editor Editing / read-only mode UI toggle
- #327538 — Revealing Markdown markers can shift content while editing
- #326539 — Agent Feedback is offered in Locked mode
- #329414 — Markdown Editor commands can now be customized with shortcuts

title: Fix section checkbox state when all items are unchecked
body:
## Summary

The Agent Customizations migration UI (introduced in #330539 / #330772, tested in #330793) groups migration candidates (e.g. Workspace/User prompt files, or Agents/Instructions) under a section with a "select all" group checkbox. Unchecking every individual item in a group was expected to also uncheck the group checkbox, but it stayed checked.

## Root cause

`renderCustomizationMigrationPage` computes each group checkbox's initial `checked` state once, from `customizations.every(...)`, when the group is rendered. Clicking the group checkbox itself triggers a full page re-render (which recomputes this correctly), but toggling an individual item's checkbox only updated the item's own state — nothing recalculated or updated the containing group's checkbox afterward, so it kept showing whatever state it had at the last full render.

## Fix

`renderSelectionCheckbox`/`renderItem` now accept an optional `onSelectionChange` callback. `renderGroup` passes a callback that recomputes `customizations.every(...)` for that group and updates `groupCheckbox.checked` accordingly, so the group checkbox stays in sync as individual items are (un)checked — without a full page re-render.

## Tests added

Added a regression test in `aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts`: `unchecking every item in a migration group unchecks the group checkbox`. It renders a group with two items, unchecks them one at a time, and asserts the group checkbox's `aria-checked` goes to `false` after the first uncheck and stays `false` after the last — then re-checking both items brings it back to `true`. Verified this test fails (group checkbox stays `true`) against the unpatched code and passes with the fix.

## Validation performed

- `scripts\test.bat --runGlob "**/aiCustomization*.test.js"` — full related suite, 61/61 passing

title: agentHost: reselect new-chat folder when its workspace folder is removed
body:
Fixes #331200

## Problem

In a multi-root Editor Window, a new (untitled) agent-host chat pins a **primary working directory** (e.g. folder `B` in a workspace `[A, B, C]`). When the user removes folder `B` from the workspace, the new Chat Editor kept showing `B` as selected — and the Folder picker could even become disabled. The not-yet-started session should instead reselect the folder a freshly created chat would pick (a still-valid sticky default, otherwise the first remaining folder `A`).

## Root cause

For an untitled chat the selected primary lives in **two** places, neither of which was invalidated on a workspace-folder change:

1. the per-session explicit selection in `AgentHostNewSessionFolderService`, and
2. the provisional backend session's immutable primary in `AgentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService` (surfaced to the chip via `getWorkingDirectory`).

Because the picker chip, config chips, and first-Send / `tryRebind` all read from these, a UI-only fix would have left the provisional session — and the first prompt — still rooted in the removed folder.

A started session is different: its working directory is the agent's fixed process root, so it must keep the removed primary (owned by `AgentHostSessionWorkingDirectorySynchronizer`, unchanged here).

## Changes

All under `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/`:

- **`agentHostNewSessionFolderService.ts`** — on `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders`, clear an explicit per-session selection whose folder is in `event.removed` and no longer present (using `extUriBiasedIgnorePathCase`). The window-level sticky default is intentionally left intact so it resurfaces if the folder is re-added. Added `resolveNewSessionPrimary()` implementing new-session precedence (valid explicit → valid sticky default → first workspace folder → `undefined`), validated against the current folders so it is order-independent between the two listeners.
- **`agentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService.ts`** — when an **untitled** draft's primary is removed, reselect via `resolveNewSessionPrimary()` and recreate the provisional at the new primary (widened `_changeWorkingDirectory` to accept `undefined` for an emptied workspace). Gated with `isUntitledChatSession` so started/rebound entries (kept in `_entries` under their real resource) keep their immutable primary and only reconcile secondaries.
- **`agentHostFolderPickerActionItem.ts`** — removed the render-time `clear()` side effect (the service now owns staleness; standalone external folders are preserved) and set the ARIA label after the visible text is written (the base derives the label from `element.textContent`, so it previously lagged one selection behind).

## Reviewer notes

- Reselection is a fall-through (default/first), not a written explicit choice, so it mirrors a brand-new chat and doesn't corrupt the sticky "last picked" default.
- Standalone folders outside the workspace are preserved: detection is gated on `event.removed`, so a folder that was never a workspace member is never treated as stale.
- The ungated `onDidChangeFolder → _changeWorkingDirectory` path stays safe for started sessions because on removal the folder service *clears* (never reselects) the selection, so it no-ops; a comment documents this coupling.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean
- Hygiene (`npm run precommit`) — clean
- Unit suites (Electron runner):
  - `agentHostNewSessionFolderService.test.ts` — 12/12 (added: removed-selection clears; sticky default survives + resurfaces on re-add; external selection preserved; `resolveNewSessionPrimary` precedence)
  - `agentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService.test.ts` — 46/46 (rewrote the test that asserted a removed primary is retained → now asserts reselection; added: single-working-directory provider reselect, zero-folders recreate, secondary-only preservation, reorder no-op, multiple drafts, started-session preservation, and a removal-racing-first-Send `tryRebind` case)
  - `agentHostChatContribution` / `agentHostGenericConfigChips` / `agentHostFolderPickerDecision` / `agentHostFolderPickerTip` — all green

title: fix: use fresh service accessor when lazily initializing chat attachment context (fixes #329610)
body:
## Summary

Opening the context menu on a chat symbol attachment (or a chat inline symbol anchor) throws `Illegal state: service accessor is only valid during the invocation of its target method`.

`hookUpSymbolAttachmentDragAndContextMenu` captures the `ServicesAccessor` passed to it via `invokeFunction`, but uses it *lazily* from inside the `ensureContextKeyService` closure, which runs on context-menu open — by then the accessor has already expired, so `accessor.get(IFileService)` inside `setResourceContext` throws.

Fixes #329610
Fixes #331400

## Root cause

Introduced by #300009, which moved the scoped context-key-service creation (and the `setResourceContext(accessor, ...)` call) out of the synchronous `invokeFunction` body and into the lazy `ensureContextKeyService` closure. The captured `accessor` is only valid during the original `invokeFunction` invocation, so the deferred `accessor.get(...)` call now throws.

## Fix

In `ensureContextKeyService`, obtain a fresh accessor by wrapping the deferred `setResourceContext` call in `instantiationService.invokeFunction(...)` instead of reusing the stale captured `accessor`. `instantiationService` is already captured at the top of the function and remains valid for the widget's lifetime — this mirrors the pattern already used a few lines above in the `dragstart` handler (`instantiationService.invokeFunction(accessor => fillEditorsDragData(...))`).

## Note for reviewers

#331414 is an open alternative fix for the same root cause (#329610) that resolves services eagerly and changes `setResourceContext`'s signature. This PR is a smaller, more surgical diff (1 line) that reuses an existing pattern in the file rather than reshaping the helper's signature — posting it so maintainers can pick whichever approach they prefer; happy to close this in favor of #331414 if that's preferred.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck-client` passes
- [x] `node build/eslint.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/attachments/chatAttachmentWidgets.ts` passes with no warnings
- [x] Manual repro: attach a symbol to chat input / get a response with an inline symbol anchor, right-click it, confirm no console error and the context menu populates resource-based actions correctly

title: agentHost: expand the legacy enterprise settings bridge
body:
## Summary

Expands the gated legacy-settings bridge (`chat.agentHost.copilot.mapLegacySettingsToManagedSettings`) beyond its initial two mappings, and clears the structural debt that made expanding it unsafe.

Refs #331143, #330349, #330472, github/copilot-sdk-internal#209

## What this does

| VS Code setting | Trigger | SDK contribution |
|---|---|---|
| `chat.tools.global.autoApprove` | policy `false` | `disableBypassPermissionsMode: 'disable'` *(existing)* |
| `chat.tools.terminal.enableAutoApprove` | `false` | `ask: ['Shell']` *(existing)* |
| `chat.agent.deniedNetworkDomains` | filter on, list populated | `deny: ['Domain(d)', …]` **(new)** |
| `chat.agent.networkFilter` | on, neither list configured | `deny: ['Domain']` **(new)** |
| `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove` | entries valued `false` | `ask: ['Shell(cmd)', …]` **(new)** |

## Why several candidate mappings were deliberately *not* added

I ran a three-model review council over the plan and cross-checked its claims against the agent runtime. Four proposed mappings turned out to be wrong, and one proposed "fix" was actively dangerous:

- **Allow-list padding was going to be the headline fix — it is a security bug.** The plan was to pad `allow` with wildcards so a restriction stayed inside its own rule family. But a covered request resolves to `managed_allow`, which the runtime returns as **approved without prompting**, and the runtime only intersects allow lists when more than one managed source supplies one. A lone list from VS Code is never intersected, so padding would have granted blanket auto-approval and could have *relaxed* an MDM policy. This bridge now never emits `allow`, and says why.
- **`chat.agent.allowedNetworkDomains`** — VS Code blocks whatever a populated allow list omits; a managed `allow` does not block what it omits, so bridging it would silently downgrade a block into a prompt.
- **`chat.tools.eligibleForAutoApproval`** — keyed on tool reference names, but the SDK only has families, so a per-tool `false` would become a family-wide restriction, and most tool names have no family at all.
- **`chat.agent.enabled`** — reviewers disagreed on the correct rule set (one flagged the proposed `Domain` deny as over-restrictive, another flagged the omission of `Read` as a file-exfiltration gap), which is itself evidence the mapping is not well-founded. VS Code already blocks these sessions host-side.
- **`chat.defaultConfiguration.approvals`** — a startup preference rather than an enterprise restriction, and `allow-auto-only` is rejected by both the SDK type and the runtime parser.
- **`chat.tools.edits.autoApprove`** — already enforced host-side with ordered last-match-wins semantics that managed rules cannot represent.

Anything requiring the SDK's per-session contract to accept more than `permissions` (MCP allow/deny lists, plugins, marketplaces, hooks, model, telemetry, sandbox, remote control) stays out of scope; those already reach the runtime through Copilot-side MDM.

## Notable corrections to the shipped behavior

- `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove: false` means *require explicit approval*, so it maps to `ask`, not `deny` — `deny` is terminal in the runtime and would remove the user's approval path.
- `Domain(*)` is not an all-domains wildcard; rule arguments are normalized as URL patterns. The kind-only `Domain` rule is the correct form.
- Rules are now deduplicated. Two settings can legitimately restrict the same operation, and duplicates were previously parsed and evaluated twice.

## Known behavior, documented rather than changed

Contributing any rule makes the runtime's managed policy active, which causes unmatched shell/read/write/URL/factory requests to require approval. That is broader than any single mapping intends, but it errs toward prompting, and the only mechanism to narrow it is the `allow` list described above. Documented in code as a deliberate tradeoff.

## Commits

Each mapping and each debt fix is a separate commit.

## Validation

- `npm run compile` — 0 errors
- `npm run test-node` — 14717 passing, 0 failing
- `npx eslint` on all changed files — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean
- 13 new unit tests covering rule validation, the new mappings, skip behavior for untranslatable input, and dedupe

## Not yet done

- Manual pass against the #331143 TPI checklist
- Gate still defaults to `false`; graduation plan not settled

title: fix: resolve services eagerly for chat symbol attachment context menu (fixes #329610)
body:
### Summary Opening the context menu on a **symbol attachment** in the chat input throws `Illegal state: service accessor is only valid during the invocation of its target method`. The context-key service for symbol attachments is initialized lazily on the first context-menu open, and that lazy closure calls `setResourceContext(accessor, ...)`, which does `accessor.get(IFileService)` on a `ServicesAccessor` whose `invokeFunction` scope has long since returned — so the accessor is no longer valid and throws. Fixes microsoft/vscode#329610 Recommended reviewer: `@roblourens` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | `1eb2581989c2` | | Author | `@roblourens` | | PR | (not resolved) | | Message | Lazy initialization of symbol attachment context key service | | Why | It moved `setResourceContext(accessor, ...)` (line 2027) into the `ensureContextKeyService` closure that runs on the CONTEXT_MENU DOM event, outside the `instantiationService.invokeFunction(...)` scope where `accessor` was created. `accessor.get()` is only valid during that invocation, so the deferred call throws "Illegal state". | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User as User participant Invoke as invokeFunction(accessor) participant Hook as hookUpSymbolAttachmentDragAndContextMenu participant Closure as ensureContextKeyService (lazy) participant Ctx as setResourceContext participant Accessor as ServicesAccessor Invoke->>Hook: accessor valid here Note over Hook: captures accessor in closure,
returns (scope ends) User->>Closure: contextmenu event (later) Closure->>Ctx: setResourceContext(accessor, ...) Ctx->>Accessor: accessor.get(IFileService) Note over Accessor: 💥 Illegal state:
accessor no longer valid ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/attachments/chatAttachmentWidgets.ts` | crash site | L2022 (from stack): `setResourceContext(accessor, ...)` inside lazy `ensureContextKeyService` | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/attachments/chatAttachmentWidgets.ts` | root cause | L2077-L2080: `setResourceContext` calls `accessor.get(IFileService/ILanguageService/IModelService)` on a captured accessor invoked after its `invokeFunction` scope ended | ### Repro Steps 1. Open the chat/agent input. 2. Attach a **symbol** (e.g. via "Add Context" → a symbol, or drag a symbol into the input). 3. Right-click the symbol attachment widget to open its context menu. 4. On first open, `ensureContextKeyService()` runs and calls `setResourceContext(accessor, ...)`, which invokes `accessor.get(IFileService)` outside the original `invokeFunction` scope → `Illegal state: service accessor is only valid during the invocation of its target method` is thrown to the unhandled-error pipeline. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — In `hookUpSymbolAttachmentDragAndContextMenu`, resolve `IFileService`, `ILanguageService`, and `IModelService` **eagerly** at the top of the function, while the `ServicesAccessor` is still valid (inside its `invokeFunction` scope). `setResourceContext` is changed to accept these already-resolved services instead of the accessor, so the lazy `ensureContextKeyService` closure no longer touches the stale accessor. This fixes the bug at its source — the invalid deferred `accessor.get()` — rather than masking it at the crash site with a try/catch (which would suppress a real "used an accessor out of scope" defect and keep it out of telemetry). The sibling `hookUpResourceAttachmentDragAndContextMenu` is updated the same way for consistency; it already resolved the context eagerly, so it only switches to passing services explicitly. **Alternatives considered** - Wrap the lazy `setResourceContext` call in a try/catch: rejected — it hides the invalid-accessor bug from telemetry instead of fixing the data producer, and the resource context would silently never be set. - Capture only the resolved `StaticResourceContextKey` inputs but keep resolving inside the closure: rejected — the closure runs outside the accessor scope by design, so any `accessor.get()` there is inherently invalid. ### Recommended Owner `@roblourens` — author of the culprit commit that introduced the lazy context-key initialization, and owner of the chat attachment widget code. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/32086779992) · opus48 · 348 AIC · ⌖ 11.9 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: agentHost: fix /fleet turn ownership after Plan → Interactive
body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8837

## Problem

Running `/fleet` immediately after switching the agent from **Plan** to **Interactive** left the chat stuck — the agent replied that plan approval was "declined twice" and the clarification UI returned "No active turn." The logs confirmed two compounding turn‑lifecycle defects in `CopilotAgentSession`, not a renderer hang:

- **RC1 — stale mode.** The effective SDK agent mode was pushed only *after* runtime slash‑command invocation (`applyMode` at the end of `_send`), and for a non‑`agent-prompt` result the early `return` skipped it entirely. So `/fleet` ran under the SDK's stale **Plan** mode and called `exit_plan_mode`.
- **RC2 — turn completed too early.** `/fleet` starts an asynchronous SDK agent loop, but the runtime `commands.invoke` returns a synchronous `completed` result. VS Code treated that as terminal, emitted `chat/turnComplete`, and cleared `_currentTurn` ~100 ms in — orphaning fleet's plan review, `ask_user`, tool calls, and final output (all emitted with an empty turn id).

## Fix (VS Code‑only, temporary)

This is a localized compatibility shim, removable once the SDK returns an `agent-prompt` result for `/fleet` from `commands.invoke`.

- **RC1:** apply the effective mode *before* invoking any non‑skill runtime command, keeping the later application so an `agent-prompt` result can still override it.
- **RC2:** route canonical built‑in `/fleet` (`kind === 'builtin' && name === 'fleet'`) through the dedicated `session.rpc.fleet.start` RPC and keep the AHP turn alive until the SDK's terminal `session.idle`.
  - Rejects attachments up front (the RPC has no attachment field).
  - Runs a shared best‑effort preflight helper `_prepareSdkTurn` (mode → permission → sandbox → MCP), used by both the normal send path and fleet — no strict/best‑effort asymmetry with a normal autopilot send.
  - Marks the turn running on `{ started: true }`, throws on `{ started: false }`/rejection while the turn is current, and treats a racing `session.idle` as authoritative (no second terminal action).
  - Guards aborts both **during preflight** (never starts the loop) and **racing the RPC** (discards the turn without a duplicate terminal action), capturing the abort token up front because an aborted idle resets the live token.

The routing intentionally bypasses `commands.invoke` invocation telemetry and `allowDuringAgentExecution` gating for `/fleet` only; this is documented at the call site as part of the temporary workaround.

## Out of scope

The independently‑confirmed empty‑turn‑id full‑message leak is tracked separately; keeping the turn alive (RC2) already prevents the primary fleet path from reaching it. This PR does not modify that handler or its tests.

## Tests

Added a `/fleet lifecycle` suite (14 cases) plus 2 RC1 mode‑ordering tests to `copilotAgentSession.test.ts`, and extended the SDK mock with `rpc.fleet.start` and an ordered RPC trace. Coverage: happy path + exactly‑once completion, strict preflight ordering, client‑`fleet` still using `commands.invoke`, alias/case + empty prompt, attachment rejection before side effects, `started:false`, RPC rejection, idle‑before‑settlement (success and late reject), aborted‑idle after start, abort racing settlement, abort during preflight, event‑id binding to the original turn (before/after RPC), and plan‑review/`ask_user` during an active fleet turn.

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p src/tsconfig.json` — clean
- `scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts` — 337 passing, 0 failing

title: fix: wrap Luna dictation alias picker endpoint in test mock (build fix for vscode-engineering#3637)

labels.name: vscode-build
labels.description: VS Code build process issues

body:
## Build failure

The unit test `LanguageModelAccess model info › publishes a core-only Luna alias for dictation cleanup without publishing hidden models directly` failed on `main`. It asserts `lunaPublishedDirectly: false` but observed `true`, so the hidden `gpt-5.6-luna` model was being published as a top-level, user-selectable language model.

## Root cause

The failure is a test-setup regression, not a production defect. In production, `AutomodeService.resolveAutoModePickerEndpoint` (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/automodeService.ts`) always wraps the chosen base endpoint in an `AutoChatEndpoint`, which is published under the pseudo model id `auto`. A hidden model such as `gpt-5.6-luna` is therefore never surfaced directly in the model picker.

The test's `IAutomodeService` mock instead returned the raw `lunaEndpoint` from `resolveAutoModePickerEndpoint`. `LanguageModelAccess._provideLanguageModelChatInfo` then pushed that hidden endpoint into the published set under its own model id `gpt-5.6-luna`, making `lunaPublishedDirectly` true. The assertion was correct; the mock was infidelitous to production behavior.

## How the fix works

The mock now mirrors production by returning a real `AutoChatEndpoint` that wraps `lunaEndpoint`. The wrapper is instantiated from the test's instantiation service (all required services — `IDomainService`, `ICAPIClientService`, etc. — are provided by `createExtensionTestingServices`) after the testing accessor is created, and assigned to the closure variable the mock returns. A base-count cache entry for the `auto` pseudo model is pre-seeded (matching the existing pattern for the other endpoints) to keep the test deterministic and fast. With the wrapper in place, the picker endpoint publishes as `auto`, `gpt-5.6-luna` is no longer published directly, and the assertion passes.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back**.

Public culprit commit/PR: `83dfbdd3a9d94908ae3c92c3ec0ca34f2afe8dcf` (PR #331338). The originating change is a legitimate feature (a core-only Luna dictation-cleanup alias); only its accompanying test mock diverged from production behavior. A fix-forward on the test is bounded and safer than reverting the feature. Owners to consult: `@meganrogge`.

## Validation

Automated validation (typecheck/test) could not be run in this environment because Node.js execution is blocked. The change was verified by source inspection against `automodeService.resolveAutoModePickerEndpoint`, `AutoChatEndpoint`, and `LanguageModelAccess._provideLanguageModelChatInfo`, confirming the mock now matches the production wrapping contract.

## Risk

Low. The change is confined to a single test file's mock setup and does not touch production code.

## Recommended reviewer

title: Tell the caller a consumed queued message was sent
body:
A message the provider consumes from the queue is reported to its caller as cancelled, and a message the provider drops is never reported at all.

### The queue has three exits and only one of them is right

`ChatService.sendRequest(..., { queue })` returns a promise that resolves when the queued message is eventually processed. Three things can retire that message, and each settles it differently:

1. **The normal dequeue** (`processNextPendingRequest`) settles it with the real send result. Correct.
2. **`removePendingRequest`** settles it as `{ kind: 'rejected', reasonCode: 'cancelled' }`. Correct for a message the user withdrew, and it is also what the agent host's server-initiated turn path calls to clear the message the provider just *consumed*, so a delivered message reports cancellation.
3. **`syncPendingRequestsFromRemote`** intends to settle anything the provider's queue no longer lists, but never does: `getPendingRequests()` returns the model's live array and `replacePendingRequests` empties it in place, so the loop that settles dropped messages iterates an array that has already been cleared. Those callers wait forever.

The root cause behind the first two is that the client has no notion of *consumed*: every route that observes a message leaving the provider's queue treats it as withdrawn.

### What callers do with it

`acceptAndAwaitSentRequest` returns `undefined`, documented as "`undefined` if it never was [sent]", and `chatSessionRoutingController._resolveQueuedCompletion` reports `{ status: 'rejected', reasonCode: 'cancelled' }`. Both describe a message that was in fact delivered and is being answered.

### The fix

- The chat service settles a consumed message where it creates the request for it, in the `onDidStartServerRequest` handler, which already receives the id the message was queued under. The completion promise is built from the response model with a listener owned by the session's store, so a session closed mid-turn does not leak it.
- `syncPendingRequestsFromRemote` takes the id of the message that became the active turn and leaves it alone. This matters independently of ordering: both the reconciliation and the server-turn detection follow the same provider state change, and their listeners run in registration order, so a fix that relied on winning that race would be fragile.
- The agent host's removal loop skips the id that is about to become the turn, so the cancel path cannot settle it first.
- `existing` is copied before `replacePendingRequests`, which makes the dropped-message settlement actually run.

Fixing the aliasing on its own would newly reject every consumed message, since the loop starts working; the consumed guard is what keeps that correct. The three tests are each tied to one of these: reverting the aliasing fix fails only the dropped-message test, reverting the consumed guard fails only the consumed-reconciliation test, and removing the settlement fails only the sent test.

Found while checking whether #330785 reusing a pending message id as the request id was safe. It is safe, and that is recorded on that PR; this is what the check turned up alongside it. It reproduces on `main` without either of my open branches, but promoting a steer into its own turn makes route 2 the ordinary path for every mid-turn message rather than an occasional one.

body: _Made it a feature request as it's barely a bug rather some design issue._ The one and only issue is exp. modern UI introduced an entire new logic which causes massive discontinuity for a user switched from original UI to exp. modern UI. So much that the user basically need to spend a lot of time restudy and rebuild ui navigation logic as if it's a completely different application. ### Tabs original/legacy: All other tabs use a different colour than main window, difference in colour naturally separates them. Selected tab using a same colour that's consistent with main window, and is visually connected with main window with no other UI elements in between. Original/Legacy theme also added a blue horizontal line on top to indicate the tab is selected, without damaging visual connection of tab with main window. exp. modern: Experimental Modern theme, however, chose to make all other tabs have the same colour as main window **EXCEPT for the one selected** And to make it worse, there're no UI elements to separate all other tabs with main window. No UI elements to separate these tabs either. But the selected one is isolated by a faint white box. Result is my brain would behave as so when looking at this: * the one with white box is treated as a button, ignored * selected tab is this giant one and somehow have 3 icons? * brain request more attention and realized that's actually 3 tabs * content in window doesn't match with tab? * brain request even more attention to check the entire tab row * realized the ignored "button" is a tab, annoyed This process occurs every time I want to switch tab. ### Side Bar **original/legacy** vs **exp. modern** -- Reduced padding made side bar icons appear more like one single element rather than individual elements. This makes users need to firstly identify icons apart from the imaginary single element, then select an icon, rather than selecting directly. ### Dividers Dividers shifted from minimal lines to a noticeable UI element, effectively fits in more UI elements without increasing amount of information displayed on screen. This change made UI feels more crowded despite might not actually reduce area for displaying contents. Dividers becoming noticeable also drains attention faster. User's brain would actively filter out these dividers, unlike those minimal thin lines which are mostly ignored. As shown in this image stolen from #330258 The bottom status bar also have a similar issue. Becoming thicker and draws more attention when user is not intended to check it. ### Conclusion So combining all of them we get a modern theme that's annoying to use.
