body:
### Summary

Opening the context menu on a chat **symbol attachment** (or a chat inline symbol anchor) throws `Illegal state: service accessor is only valid during the invocation of its target method`. The `hookUpSymbolAttachmentDragAndContextMenu` helper captures the `ServicesAccessor` passed to it via `invokeFunction`, but then uses it *lazily* from inside a deferred `ensureContextKeyService` closure that runs on context-menu open. By that time the accessor has already expired (`_done === true`), so `accessor.get(IFileService)` inside `setResourceContext` throws. Impact: ~479 users on 1.132.0; the context menu fails to populate resource context keys.

Fixes microsoft/vscode\#329610
Recommended reviewer: `@roblourens`

### Culprit Commit

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Commit | [`1eb2581989c2`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/1eb2581989c23047ff009b68e910e48f51d4d3d7) |
| Author | `@roblourens` |
| PR | #300009 |
| Message | Optimize chat anchor widget (#300009) — Lazily create scoped CKS: this can be expensive and is not needed until the context menu is shown |
| Why | This commit moved the scoped context-key-service creation (and the `setResourceContext(accessor, ...)` call) out of the synchronous `invokeFunction` body and into the lazy `ensureContextKeyService` closure, which runs on context-menu open. The captured `accessor` is only valid during the original `invokeFunction` invocation, so the deferred `accessor.get(...)` in `setResourceContext` now throws. |

### Code Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Init as invokeFunction(hookUp)
    participant Closure as ensureContextKeyService (deferred)
    participant SetCtx as setResourceContext
    participant Accessor as ServicesAccessor

    Init->>Closure: capture accessor, register contextmenu listener
    Note over Init: invokeFunction returns, accessor marked _done=true
    Note over Closure: Root cause: lazy closure reuses the expired accessor
    Closure->>SetCtx: setResourceContext(accessor, ...)
    SetCtx->>Accessor: accessor.get(IFileService)
    Note over Accessor: Error thrown: service accessor only valid during invocation
```

### Affected Files

| File | Role | Evidence |
|------|------|----------|
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/attachments/chatAttachmentWidgets.ts` | crash site | L2078 `accessor.get(IFileService)` inside `setResourceContext` |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/attachments/chatAttachmentWidgets.ts` | root cause | L2018-L2024: `ensureContextKeyService` lazy closure called `setResourceContext(accessor, ...)` after the enclosing `invokeFunction` had returned and the accessor expired |
| `src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiationService.ts` | throw site | `if (_done) throw illegalState('service accessor is only valid during the invocation of its target method')` |

### Repro Steps

1. Open Chat and get a response containing an inline symbol anchor, or add a symbol attachment to the chat input.
2. Right-click the symbol anchor / attachment widget to open its context menu (first open triggers the lazy `ensureContextKeyService`).
3. Observe the unhandled error `Illegal state: service accessor is only valid during the invocation of its target method` in telemetry / dev-tools console.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** — in `ensureContextKeyService`, obtain a *fresh* accessor by wrapping the deferred `setResourceContext` call in `instantiationService.invokeFunction(...)` instead of reusing the stale captured `accessor`:

```ts
instantiationService.invokeFunction(accessor => setResourceContext(accessor, scopedContextKeyService!, attachment.value.uri));
```

`instantiationService` is already captured at the top of the function and remains valid for the widget's lifetime. This is exactly the same pattern already used a few lines above in the `dragstart` handler (`instantiationService.invokeFunction(accessor => fillEditorsDragData(...))`), so it is consistent with the surrounding code. The fix is applied at the data producer — the lazy closure that supplies the expired accessor to `setResourceContext` — rather than guarding or wrapping the crash site inside `setResourceContext`, following the principle of fixing at the producer of the invalid data rather than the crash site.

**Alternatives considered**: passing `IFileService`/`ILanguageService`/`IModelService` down as pre-resolved services instead of an accessor — rejected as more invasive (it would change `setResourceContext`'s signature and every caller) for no benefit over re-invoking `invokeFunction`.

**Why this fix**: after this change, `chatAttachmentWidgets.ts:2022` no longer reads services from the expired captured accessor; `setResourceContext` receives a live accessor scoped to a fresh `invokeFunction` invocation, so `accessor.get(...)` cannot hit the `_done` illegal-state branch.

### Recommended Owner

`@roblourens` — author of the culprit commit `1eb2581989c2` (PR #300009) that introduced the lazy context-key-service initialization; core VS Code chat area owner, with write access and recent commit activity in the last 90 days.

body:
## Build failure

The unit test `LanguageModelAccess model info › publishes a core-only Luna alias for dictation cleanup without publishing hidden models directly` failed on `main`. It asserts `lunaPublishedDirectly: false` but observed `true`, so the hidden `gpt-5.6-luna` model was being published as a top-level, user-selectable language model.

## Root cause

The failure is a test-setup regression, not a production defect. In production, `AutomodeService.resolveAutoModePickerEndpoint` (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/automodeService.ts`) always wraps the chosen base endpoint in an `AutoChatEndpoint`, which is published under the pseudo model id `auto`. A hidden model such as `gpt-5.6-luna` is therefore never surfaced directly in the model picker.

The test's `IAutomodeService` mock instead returned the raw `lunaEndpoint` from `resolveAutoModePickerEndpoint`. `LanguageModelAccess._provideLanguageModelChatInfo` then pushed that hidden endpoint into the published set under its own model id `gpt-5.6-luna`, making `lunaPublishedDirectly` true. The assertion was correct; the mock was infidelitous to production behavior.

## How the fix works

The mock now mirrors production by returning a real `AutoChatEndpoint` that wraps `lunaEndpoint`. title: Report vision support for natively served Claude models
body:
Fixes #331347.

A pasted image in a Claude session on the native (BYO-Anthropic) transport is attached, sent, and understood by the model, but the UI marks it unsupported: the attachment renders with a warning icon and the hover reads "*{model}* does not support images." Users conclude the attachment was dropped and stop pasting images.

`fromSdkModelInfo` hardcoded the capability:

```ts
supportsVision: false,
```

while the CAPI projection directly above it reads the real one (`supportsVision: !!supports?.vision`), so the two transports disagreed about the same underlying models.

`ModelInfo` in `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` has no vision field at all. It carries `supportsEffort`, `supportedEffortLevels`, `supportsAdaptiveThinking`, `supportsFastMode` and `supportsAutoMode`, and nothing about image input. So `false` was standing in for "the SDK does not say", but it does not read that way downstream: `agentHostLanguageModelProvider` collapses the value to a boolean (`vision: m.supportsVision ?? false`) and `chatAttachmentWidgets` treats it as authoritative, so "unknown" became a positive claim that the model cannot accept images.

Leaving the field unset changes nothing for the same reason, which makes `true` the accurate answer for this transport: every row it offers is a Claude model, and image input is available across them. The comment says so at the seam, so whoever adds a real capability to `ModelInfo` can replace it with the actual signal.

The existing projection test asserted the old value and now asserts the new one, with a note about why.

title: agents window: fix sessions list progress
body:
## Summary

Fixes Sessions list progress indicators becoming stale in either direction:

- a session is running, but the list does not show a spinner;
- a session has completed, but the list continues showing a spinner.

## Root cause

The Agent Host correctly aggregated chat activity into the session status, but did not publish the resulting session-summary updates for sessions initially returned by `root/listSessions`.

A recent publication filter only emitted `root/sessionSummaryChanged` for sessions recorded as published. That record was updated for `root/sessionAdded`, but not for `root/listSessions`. As a result, restored/listed sessions were visible to the client while the host still treated their summaries as unpublished.

The subscribed chat continued receiving live `session/chatUpdated` actions, so the chat content showed the correct state. The Sessions list depended on the suppressed root summary update and retained its previous state, producing the mismatch.

## Fix

- Record summaries returned by `root/listSessions` as published without emitting redundant `root/sessionAdded` notifications.
- Preserve the listed summary as the notification-diff baseline so subsequent status and activity changes are emitted normally.
- Keep filtered sessions unpublished, preserving the existing external-session visibility behavior.
- Remove the client-side status recomputation workaround; the UI now consumes the status published by the Agent Host.
- Add a protocol-level regression test covering a restored session returned by `listSessions` and its subsequent transition to in progress.

This pull request addresses several UX concerns and accessibility regressions related to the chat sticky scroll feature. Key changes include:

- **Corrected sticky header behavior**: One-turn chats now correctly display a sticky header, independent of the previous two-prompt minimum requirement.
- **Accurate prompt selection**: The logic for determining which prompt owns the sticky header has been refined to ensure the correct prompt is displayed based on its position in the viewport.
- **Improved handling of multiple visible turns**: The header now behaves consistently when multiple prompts are visible, preventing incorrect replacements or hiding.
- **Fixed header transition issues**: The outgoing label remains visible during transitions, eliminating any flashing of the incoming prompt.
- **Exclusion of system-generated requests**: System notifications are no longer counted as user prompts, ensuring clarity in the prompt timeline.
- **Accessibility improvements**: Removed outdated instructions regarding navigation buttons from the accessibility help, aligning it with the current UI.

Additionally, focused tests have been added to validate these changes, ensuring robust coverage for the new behavior. All relevant tests have passed successfully.
